timeline.ruleset: Expert Rules introduced in parallel with Official Rules

rule_boundary.expert_rules_evidence: A strong later reconstruction dates Expert Rules to May 5, 1999 and says recognized tournaments used them, but it also explicitly says the first publication source has not been located. The Tokyo Dome event page identifies the event and distributed cards but does not identify its rulebook or event regulations. Therefore Expert Rules are the best working hypothesis, not a proven event fact.

recertification_2026_08.purpose: An independent five-agent audit (Konami-chronology, early-promo/tournament, card-identity, adversarial-test, community-pool comparator roles) found primary-source contradictions in the original 2026-08 certification (commit 6f937e62b29b2edfcf2366a73017ba3e7635cf84). This block records exactly what changed and what did not.
recertification_2026_08.deleted_product_reason: Fabricated: claimed a physical ocg-jp release on 1999-02-21 of Millennium Shield/Megasonic Eye/Yamadron. This was a misreading of a Yugipedia results table (two columns, 'Physical card'/'Video game card', by National Tournament placement tier); the Qualifying tier's Physical-card cell is blank, and its Video-game-card cell (which does include these 3 names, alongside Kanan the Swordmistress) links to Yu-Gi-Oh! Duel Monsters (Game Boy, 1998-12-16, itself Non-OCG) hidden-card-unlock pages, not physical OCG cards. Konami's official product catalogue has no row for any such product, and each of the 3 cards' own Konami card-level print-history shows no printing earlier than 1999-06-01. Kanan the Swordmistress is unaffected: she is physically real via the separate, correctly-sourced yu-gi-oh-duel-monsters-national-tournament-attendance-card product, confirmed directly against Konami.

recertification_2026_08.pool_unchanged_explanation: None of the three corrections removed a card's availability before the 1999-08-25 cutoff: the two Game Guide date fixes both remain pre-cutoff, and the three cards from the deleted product remain correctly available via their genuine 1999-06-01 Limited Edition pack release. The pool's digest is a checksum of {passcode, name} pairs only, never dates or source products, so it structurally could not have caught either defect - this recertification's real regression protection is tests/fixtures/ocg1999-official-chronology.json (an evidence base independent of this repository's own product files) plus tests/test_ocg1999_release_certification.py's fixture-comparison and adversarial tests, not the pool digest.
